Any body thought about below:

Build a standalone theorem based on the mathlib4 source. Let AI learn directly from how native mathlib4 code is written, so it can generate human-readable code in the proper style. This could address the pass@k problem by reducing cost and eliminating bad syntax generation
I would be surprised if mathlib isn't already part of the training data of many AI

Current training data is by raw type or called expanding item. The purposal is: entire data completely as same as source code with: 1. Address environment issue. 2. Replace with explicit like using simp only. 3. Figure out each statement dependency
I am not convinced that is the only training data. There is even #43408 that just makes changes at syntax level to influence the training data

Not change mathlib4 source code, give another additional data with source code for training. It can use for vs code on message. So that additional data set could be additional information to reduce AI guessing and even developer guessing in vs code.
